name: Terrera Mountain
_turns: How many turns a game lasts (the arena doc); the turn track at the table's end has a slot for each.
_grid: One character per tile, row 0 = the far side (player 2), last row = player 1's side. Each character is defined in the legend. From a photo of the user's three drawn boards (mapstomake/Terrera Mountain.webp, taken sideways: turned upright, each board perspective-straightened). Columns 0-7: the centre (8x16, both players' spawns, 2 flags). Columns 9-16: the two side floors (8x8 each), side by side with the centre like Yaksha's boxes (the pillars take the left strip): the top floor in rows 0-7, the bottom floor in rows 8-15. Column 8 is the strip between them: a ridge of rock at the centre's height (level 1) that nothing stands on (the user: an empty gap looked odd); the board is centred on it, so the point where all three boards meet is the middle of the table (the user's choice). Tunnels 1-4 link the centre with each floor (the d4 roll picks the exit).
_legend: level = height step (0 = lowest; "raise" lifts whole boards). surface picks the look. marker = something on the tile (painted, or a 3D piece with piece: true). n/s/e/w and a/b/c/d (nw/ne/sw/se) = quicksand, the arrow the way it drags a grounded Pokemon. P/Q/R/S = tunnel mouths 1-4; on the side floors the numbered corners are quicksand too (J 1 nw, I 2 ne, G 3 se, H 4 sw). Z = control zone (a 4x4 frame); X = its hatched middle (cracked: you fall through to the floor below). F = flag.
_raise: Heights, slightly different per board (the user): bottom floor at the table (level 0), the centre one level up, the top floor two.
_board: The published board files the map picker uses (from tools/build_board.py; update when a new version is published), then run tools/build_arena_index.py.
_table: Image for the table around the board (placeholder until the arena gets its own).
_textures: Placeholders from tools/draw_placeholders.py: hive earth, quicksand, layered earth cliffs.
